key_insight: Diffusion LMs can finish many tokens well before the final denoising step; by detecting convergence at each token during inference, you can stop refining those tokens early without retraining the model.
problem_solved: Iterative denoising in diffusion language models is computationally inefficient because tokens often stabilize long before the full number of refinement steps, wasting compute, latency, and energy.
method: Training-free, token-level early stopping: monitor each position independently during inference and decide when a token has converged.
Use lightweight signals derived from the model's own predictions and local context (e.g., prediction consistency, local confidence) to detect per-token convergence.
Dynamically finalize tokens as soon as they meet convergence criteria and skip further denoising for those positions while continuing refinement elsewhere.
impact: Enables lower-latency, more compute- and energy-efficient text generation from diffusion LMs without retraining, making diffusion-based inference more practical for deployment and high-throughput applications.
visual_elements: Timeline/sequence diagram showing denoising steps with tokens 'freezing' at different times (token-level stop points)
Schematic flowchart: model predictions → lightweight signal extraction → per-token convergence decision → finalize token
Before/after bar chart comparing total inference steps or compute with and without token-level early stopping
Heatmap over time vs. sequence position indicating when each token converges (visualizing per-token variability)
paper_title: Just on Time: Token-Level Early Stopping for Diffusion Language Models
paper_authors: Zahar Kohut, Severyn Shykula, Dmytro Khamula, Mykola Vysotskyi, Taras Rumezhak
